before.name: c. 2900+ BC Prometheus would have sprouted in this century

after.name: Prometheus pine: older possible germination estimate; same tree as c. 2880, date uncertain

r2SourceEvidence.review_note: The 30th-century page gives c.2900+ BCE with the tree sprouting within that century; the 29th-century and Methuselah pages give an estimated c.2880 BCE. Both refer to the same pine WPN-114, not two separate germinations. Prometheus was felled in 1964. Wikipedia reports 4,862 rings counted at about 2.5 m above the germination point, with missing rings and time to reach that height uncertain; one interpretation suggests at least 5,000 years old at felling. NPS gives 4,862 rings and an age estimate of 4,900, with uncertainty about missing rings. Neither 3000 nor 2880 is an established exact sprouting year. The existing one-year slots are approximate references reflecting differing estimates, not separate events or a scientific age range. Retained map pin is a regional Wheeler Peak reference, not a verified tree location. The 1964 cutting is not an event in these BCE slots.
r2SourceEvidence.date_precision: Approximate and disputed germination, with both entries referring to the same individual tree.
r2SourceEvidence.location_precision: Wheeler Peak area reference only, not verified exact stump coordinate; radius is a game setting.
